blog/cost-segregation-retail-properties/.title: Retail Center Cost Segregation Studies | Stratum
blog/cost-segregation-retail-properties/.description: Review a retail-center cost segregation study: tenant improvements, shared systems, property records, commercial study scope and a written proposal.
blog/cost-segregation-retail-properties/.heading: Request a retail-center study scope
blog/cost-segregation-retail-properties/.body:
Bring the property address, rent roll or use map, closing records, improvement history and existing depreciation schedule. Confirm how tenant-funded improvements and shared systems will be documented and reconciled before commissioning the study.

Review commercial building study services and compare the proposed inspection, technical review, asset schedules and preparer handoff.

blog/cost-segregation-apartment-building.title: Apartment Cost Segregation: Study Scope | Stratum
blog/cost-segregation-apartment-building.description: Evaluate apartment and multifamily cost segregation: unit variations, common areas, renovation history, documentation and a property-specific study quote.
blog/cost-segregation-apartment-building.heading: Prepare an apartment-building study review
blog/cost-segregation-apartment-building.body:
Provide unit counts and layouts, renovation dates, common-area inventories and existing asset schedules. Ask how any representative-unit sampling will account for differences across the property.

Review multifamily and apartment study services, then discuss your building and proposed scope.

blog/cost-segregation-medical-office-bui.title: Medical Office Cost Segregation Studies | Stratum
blog/cost-segregation-medical-office-bui.description: Review medical-office cost segregation, specialized systems, ownership of improvements, property documentation and the scope of a commercial study.
blog/cost-segregation-medical-office-bui.heading: Define your medical-office study scope
blog/cost-segregation-medical-office-bui.body:
Identify who owns the building, equipment and tenant improvements. Bring plans, improvement invoices, purchase records and existing depreciation schedules so the study team can distinguish shared building systems from property-specific components.

Review commercial study services and request a property-specific scope discussion. Confirm return implementation and any separately engaged tax work.
